description: NeuraSilicon Space AI is a team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to develop an AI-powered platform for analyzing NASA microgravity combustion data and improving space mission fire safety. Our skills include Python, AI/ML, GPU computing, VLSI, and data analysis. We welcome AI researchers, developers, data scientists, and space enthusiasts.
summary:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive research dashboard that analyzes NASA's PSI-69 Flame Extinguishment (FLEX) experimental dataset to explore flame behavior and fire-extinguishment outcomes in microgravity.

The project transforms experimental data into accessible visual insights through exploratory data analysis, statistical analysis, machine-learning evaluation, explainability, and an interactive prediction lab. It examines experimental outcomes including extinction, disruption, and completion, while exploring relationships between combustion conditions and observed results.

Built with Python, Streamlit, pandas, and scikit-learn, the dashboard helps users investigate the experimental evidence and understand the limitations of predictive modeling. Its goal is to make NASA combustion research more accessible and support further investigation into fire safety for future space missions.
details:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive research platform developed to explore NASA's PSI-69 Version 5 Flame Extinguishment (FLEX) experimental dataset. The project focuses on understanding flame behavior and experimental outcomes under microgravity conditions.

The dashboard contains eight sections:

  1. Research Overview
  2. Experimental Data Explorer
  3. Exploratory Data Analysis
  4. Statistical Analysis
  5. Model Evaluation
  6. Explainability & Errors
  7. Data Quality & Limitations
  8. Prediction Lab

The project analyzes 274 experimental records, with 273 records used for predictive modeling after excluding one record with invalid ambient-pressure data. The outcome categories include Extinction, Disruption, and Completion.

A date-grouped Random Forest evaluation achieved 76.92% accuracy, 57.76% balanced accuracy, and 58.41% macro F1. The dashboard also highlights class imbalance and limitations in predicting less-represented outcomes.

Technologies used include Python, Streamlit, pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, and data visualization tools.

The project is a research prototype. Its predictions are exploratory and are not validated for operational spacecraft fire-safety decisions. Its purpose is to make experimental research accessible, encourage scientific investigation, and support future research into combustion and fire safety in space.
